issues.legal_issue: An injunction suit against an encroacher is not defeated by a technical discrepancy between the plaintiff identified in an amendment and the plaintiff found to be in possession when the pleadings, read as a whole, permit relief based on the possession of any plaintiff.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought mandatory and permanent injunctions to remove fencing and thorny bushes erected on land they claimed to possess.

The plaintiffs amended their pleadings to avoid litigating their competing claims to title and agreed that relief, if justified, could be granted in favour of the plaintiff claiming as the next reversioner.
The trial court found that one plaintiff was in possession and that the defendant had neither title nor possession and had encroached on the land; the appellate court affirmed those findings.
The High Court dismissed the suit because the plaintiff found to be in possession was not the plaintiff identified in the amendment as entitled to relief.
issues.conclusion: The amendment, construed liberally, included the possession found by the courts below and did not prevent an injunction. The appeal was allowed, the High Court judgment was set aside, and the trial court decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit to remove an encroachment, the plaintiffs need show that the land was in the possession of a plaintiff or any of them and that the defendant encroached on it; competing claims to title among the plaintiffs are immaterial to relief against the defendant. Pleadings should be construed broadly rather than technically, and possession by one plaintiff may be treated as possession on behalf of another where the pleadings and circumstances support that construction. The judgment cites no statutory provisions or earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: injunction_suit and defendant_encroached and a_plaintiff_in_possession and defendant_lacks_title_and_possession and pleadings_permit_relief_for_actual_possessor

predicates.injunction_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking an injunction against an alleged encroachment.
predicates.defendant_encroached: The defendant erected or placed an obstruction on land possessed by the plaintiff or plaintiffs.
predicates.a_plaintiff_in_possession: At least one plaintiff was found to possess the disputed land.
predicates.defendant_lacks_title_and_possession: The defendant was found to have neither title to nor possession of the disputed land.
predicates.pleadings_permit_relief_for_actual_posse: The pleadings, read as a whole, permit relief based on the possession of the plaintiff found to possess the land, despite any different identification of the person entitled to relief.

issues.definition: When an injunction suit concerns an encroachment by a defendant lacking title and possession, and a plaintiff possesses the land and the pleadings permit relief for that possessor, the rule grants an injunction.
